---
title: "Learning Portfolio"
---

## Why a portfolio?

Weekly activities produce evidence of how your computational reasoning develops. After the midterm, selected evidence will be combined into a diagnostic portfolio.

The portfolio is designed to answer a more useful question than:

> “What is my average score?”

It asks:

> “Which computational skills are becoming secure, and where do I still need deliberate practice?”

## Core skill dimensions

| Tag | Skill | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **REP** | Representation | identifying data, state, input, output, and computational structure |
| **TRC** | Code reading & tracing | predicting how code changes state and produces output |
| **CTL** | Control flow | reasoning about sequence, conditions, and repetition |
| **DEC** | Decomposition | breaking a larger problem into manageable parts |
| **DBG** | Testing & debugging | locating errors and verifying behaviour |
| **TRN** | Domain transfer | applying computational patterns to new economics/business/data contexts |

## Evidence sources

Your portfolio may include:

- quiz responses;
- selected lab evidence;
- exit tickets;
- homework tasks;
- self-assessment;
- recurring misconception patterns.

## What feedback can look like

A portfolio may identify:

- **secure skills**;
- **developing skills**;
- **recurring misconceptions**;
- **recommended next practice**;
- differences between **self-perception and observed evidence**.

Individual student data are **not published on this website**.
